ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume rationale is type transparency - allowing wallets to display actual struct contents to users instead of opaque hex strings.

ambiguities.text: Security considerations marked 'Needs discussion'—threat model undefined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard EIP-712 threat model applies, plus considerations for type confusion between outer and inner schemas.

ambiguities.text: No specification for nested boxes (can boxes contain boxes?)
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume nested boxes are not supported in initial specification; inner types cannot use box keyword.
Assume type schemas are immutable once deployed; versioning handled at application level.
Assume standard EIP-712 domain separator provides replay protection; box mechanism does not change this.

implicit_assumptions.description: Wallets implement EIP-712 and can parse JSON structures for type definitions
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Boxed values would be displayed as opaque data, defeating the purpose of the extension

implicit_assumptions.description: Keccak256 hashing remains consistent across all implementations
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Signature verification would fail between different implementations

implicit_assumptions.description: Type name collisions between outer and inner schemas are managed by the application
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Type confusion could lead to incorrect hash computation or display

implicit_assumptions.description: The specification assumes deterministic type ordering and encoding
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Different implementations could produce different hashes for the same message

implicit_assumptions.description: Users understand that boxed contents are signed along with outer struct
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users might not realize they are committing to inner content, leading to unexpected signed commitments
